object_rule: Valyrian manufactured objects must look **used, not treasured** - no polish, gemstones, display lighting or heraldry. Gold is tarnished except where hands have worn it bright. A weapon of state kept in a store-room, not a relic in a shrine.

batch_053_note: The scream. Physical cost, not magic: 0521 from under the bell with smoke drawn out and nothing glowing, 0523 as pure throat-and-jaw anatomy cropped so no face exists, 0524's mouthpiece crusted with a ring of dry salt deposit, 0525 a still figure far from the horn on a terrace, 0526 one horn still standing while the city is gone, 0527's bell crushed and split, 0528 hauling one out of fused ruins, 0529 chapped and blistered lips with no burn, 0530 a heaving chest and a face lost in a hood.
the_scream_rule: The scream is physical cost, not magic. Show flush, taut tendons, sweat, a worn and crusted mouthpiece, dry residue - then a still body on a terrace and one whole horn standing among ruins a civilisation later. No aura, no glow, no shockwave, no sound effect, nothing alight, in any frame.
the_body_rule: No face and no injury in batch 053. Strain is tendons, flush and sweat; damage is dryness, salt deposit and worn metal; the cost is posture. Negations carried in every prompt: no blood, no wound, no injury, no bruise, no burn. This is also why the batch cleared moderation on the first pass: describe what the body is doing, not what has been done to it.

batch_055_note: Batch 055 'The Book Nobody Kept' (18:00-18:20) CLOSED 10/10. The batch changes the episode's voice: from here the narration leaves Valyria's own procedure and enters a dispute about the past (Septon Barth, ~4,000 years later, whose Unnatural History was burned). Rule (bible 4h): the past is never rendered as truth, only as testimony — no glowing script, no floating glyphs, no altar tableau, no centred mage. Five rejections across three frames and one transport failure: 0543 pass 1 (a distant seated figure resolved into a clean profile at 6x), 0545 pass 1 (fingertips rendered deep red, reading as raw flesh at 4x), 0546 (no image returned by the first call; retry landed first look), 0548 pass 1 (ear resolved crisply at 3x under a turned-away head), 0548 pass 2 (bare shoulder and neck in the left margin, robe fallen away). 0548 pass 3 removes the person entirely — the empty pushed-back stool, worn smooth, is the batch's best frame.
the_testimony_rule: The past is never rendered as truth, only as testimony. Barth is the frame, not the subject. Where Valyria appears it is small, partial or mediated: a wall the spells were spoken against, a city four thousand years dead, a woman seen only from behind. No full-stage altar tableau, no centred mage, no glowing script.
batch_055_detail_lesson: Two rules were enforced in the composition and then violated in the detail this batch: a face at the far end of a table, an injury in a fingertip. Neither was visible at frame size; both were caught at 4x-6x. Crop the head region AND skin contact points (hands, fingertips) before approving.
batch_055_face_rule_lesson: The no-face rule is a CROP check, not a framing instruction, and it now has a second clause. (1) The head must be OUTSIDE the frame or fully turned away — 0548 pass 1 proved that a turned-away head still ships an ear at 3x. (2) The fallback 'show only a shoulder or a hand' has its own failure mode: skin at the edge of frame is still a body, and a body without its robe is a continuity error rather than a camera angle (0548 pass 2). The reliable answer is to photograph the wear, not the wearer.
fire_containment_rule: Fire is permitted only where a hand built a place to hold it, and the frame must show the containment as clearly as the fire. 0546's burning manuscripts survive the batch's no-glow rule because every flame is hand-sized and inside a stone-lined font — no blaze, no fireball, no embers, no glow in the ash.
